One Likelihood Statistic for One Coefficient

Source: R/restricted.R
statmod_stat_at.Rd

Computes the Wald, likelihood-ratio, Rao score or Terrell gradient statistic for the hypothesis that one coefficient equals value, with its p-value.

Usage

statmod_stat_at(
  fit,
  param,
  coefname,
  value = 0,
  test = wald_test(),
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  mode_error = FALSE,
  objective0 = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

param, coefname

Which coefficient, as in statmod_restrict().

value

The value under the null, a single number. The default is 0.

test

A test_statistic object: wald_test(), lr_test(), score_test() or gradient_test().

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance that the Wald statistic reads, as vcov.StatmodFit() takes it.

mode_error

Whether to read how far above its mode the restricted fit stopped (restricted_mode_error()). The default is FALSE, because reading it costs one Hessian where the likelihood ratio and the gradient statistic need none. summary.StatmodFit(), which calls this once per row, and statmod_invert(), which calls it once per evaluation of the statistic, do not read it.

objective0

The penalized objective at the unrestricted joint mode, as joint_objective() returns it, for a caller that reads the likelihood ratio many times on one fit. NULL computes it here.

Value

A list with test (the test_statistic object), statistic, df, p.value, converged – NA for the Wald statistic and the restricted fit's flag for the other three – and mode_error, NA unless it is requested.

Details

All four read the penalized objective, which is the function that the fit maximizes. Writing \(\ell_p(\beta) = \ell(\beta) - \rho(\beta;\theta)\) for it, \(\hat\beta\) for the unrestricted estimates, \(\tilde\beta\) for the estimates in which \(\beta_j\) is held at \(b\), \(U = \partial\ell_p\) for its score and \(K\) for the penalized information, the four are $$W = (\hat\beta_j - b)^2 / \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta_j), \qquad LR = 2\{\ell_p(\hat\beta) - \ell_p(\tilde\beta)\},$$ $$S = U_j(\tilde\beta)^2 \, [K(\tilde\beta)^{-1}]_{jj}, \qquad T = U_j(\tilde\beta)\,(\hat\beta_j - b),$$ each compared with a \(\chi^2_1\). Where the model carries no penalty \(\ell_p\) is the log-likelihood and these are the classical four.

The score statistic has the general form \(U'K^{-1}U\). It reduces to the product above because every other component of \(U\) vanishes at the restricted maximum, which also indicates that the restricted fit has converged.

The penalized objective and the likelihood

The likelihood ratio is taken on \(\ell_p\) and not on \(\ell\). \(\tilde\beta\) maximizes \(\ell_p\) under the restriction and not \(\ell\), so \(\ell(\tilde\beta)\) can exceed \(\ell(\hat\beta)\) and the difference of log-likelihoods can be negative. The other three statistics read the penalized objective as well: \(U\) and \(K\) are its gradient and its curvature, and the Wald variance is \((H+S)^{-1}\) under vcov_type = bayesian_vcov().

For a shrunk coordinate this is the reading that vcov.StatmodFit() gives under vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(): the penalty is a log-prior, so \(\ell_p\) is a log posterior at the hyperparameters in force, and the interval by inversion is the set that the posterior does not reject, conditional on them. The interpretation that the Wald interval on such a row carries therefore extends to the other three statistics. On a smooth the inverted interval and the Wald one agree to second order, and the inversion adds the asymmetry.

Differences between the statistics

The Wald statistic reads only the unrestricted fit and needs no refit, which is why the summary reports it by default. It depends on how the parameter is written: a nonlinear reparametrization of the coefficient changes it, whereas the likelihood ratio, a difference of objective values at the same two points, is not changed. The Wald statistic also loses power against a distant alternative (the Hauck-Donner effect), because the curvature is read at \(\hat\beta\) rather than under the null.

The gradient statistic needs the restricted fit and no matrix inversion: it is the score contracted with the distance between the two fits.

See also

statmod_restrict(), which the three restricted statistics read.
